dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Coloring » Nowhere-zero flows
dossier_meta.statement_text: Conjecture Every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 5-flow.
dossier_meta.context_text: For planar graphs , this theorem follows from flow/coloring duality , and the Five color theorem (every loopless planar graph is 5-colorable). In light of this, we may view this conjecture as a widesweeping generalization of the 5-color-theorem. The Petersen graph does not have a nowhere-zero 4-flow, which shows that this conjecture (if true) is best possible. It is far from obvious that there should exist a fixed number $ k $ so that every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero $ k $ -flow. Indeed, this weaker conjecture was also made by Tutte, but was resolved by Kilpatrick [K] and independently Jaeger [J], who both proved that bridgeless graphs have nowhere-zero 8-flows. Seymour [S] improved upon this result by showing that bridgeless graphs have nowhere-zero 6-flows.
